findings.finding: The change is safe because the identity line never enters context.items or the Responses input, so no checkpoint stores it and no later turn replays it. providers.ts builds the Gateway checkpoint from context.items plus the assistant text and puts the line only in the request array. responses.ts sends the line as the top-level instructions field, outside the input that trimCompacted keeps. A mutation in the lane proved the Gateway half. With the line added to the Gateway checkpoint, identity.test.ts failed only the test that a kimi reply never saves its identity into the checkpoint, with the diff 'Expected substring: not "running in the Glow app"', and the received checkpoint JSON held the system item. After the file was restored to the committed version, all 7 tests passed.
findings.none: The fact holds at the committed head.

findings.finding: Grep stops at the wire, so the request shape was read in the source. context.items never holds a system item, because the only other system textItem is the Kimi summary request in compaction/context.ts, and the summary comes back into the context as a user item. A Gateway reply therefore sends exactly one system message. The Kimi summary already sends a system message with array content through the same gatewayMessages mapping. DeepSeek replies send a system message for the first time. Whether every Gateway upstream accepts it, and whether Gateway chunks carry a top-level model, is unverified live. A chunk without a model only makes the log show answered=-.
findings.none: The fakes cover the request shape, and a live check needs a paid call that this change may not make. The next approved live check covers it.

findings.finding: docs/providers.md is the controls path that routed this skill. No tool or workflow parses it. A grep of tools/ and .github/ finds it only as a path fixture in tools/__tests__/routing-committed.test.js and in skill records, so the docs change cannot change what any check passes.
findings.none: Prose only, with no reader in the checks.

findings.finding: The answered value is logged as the provider sends it. A model string with a newline would split the log line. The likelihood is low because the value is a provider model id, and the cost is a misleading log line, never a failed reply.
findings.none: Log-only impact with a low likelihood. A follow-up can restrict the value to an id pattern if wanted.

findings.finding: The try/catch around JSON.parse in reportedModel is not defensive slop. Every raw chunk passes through the reader, and the Gateway stream ends with a [DONE] record that is not JSON. The diff adds no comments, no any casts, and no nesting beyond the style of the file.
comment-sicko was not spawned, because the rules for this lane allow only one subagent type. The same scope, the diff against origin/main, was checked directly.
findings.none: The direct check below covers the scope.

findings.finding: A grep of the added lines for line comments, block comments, lint disables, and TypeScript suppressions found none. The only match was a ws:// URL in the test fixture.

identity.test.ts was run on the committed head and passed 7 of 7. The mutation red quoted above names the predicted disagreement, the checkpoint holding the identity line, and not an exception or an empty result.
findings.none: The tests prove the claims they name.

findings.finding: The docs say the label is the one the phone shows. models.ts builds each catalog entry with label: models[entry.model].label, so the identity line and the picker read the same registry field.

The new section in docs/providers.md is reference. It describes the request contents and the log format, with no instruction and no opinion, and it uses the real field names instructions, system, and response.model.
One parenthesis lists where the model id comes from as two noun phrases rather than a full sentence. It reads one way and does not mislead.
findings.cites: Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)
findings.none: Cosmetic, and rewording it would churn an accurate sentence.

findings.finding: One alternative was to add a model field to ProviderChunk and fill it where gateway.ts and responses.ts already parse each chunk. That would drop modelReportSchema and the second parse. It also changes a shared type and both clients, and the current reader stops parsing after the first chunk that reports a model. The saving is small, so it is not a missed simplification.
findings.none: The current shape is smaller and keeps the change in one file.

findings.finding: The private reply method repeats the seven parameters of generate. The alternatives were a mutable completion across both wire branches or a log call in each branch. No file nears 1000 lines (providers.ts has 155), and no branch was added to an unrelated flow.
findings.none: No blocker. The wrapper is the smallest way to log once after both branches.

findings.finding: Two log tests share the title "a finished kimi reply logs the requested and answered model, never message text". The second covers the case with no reported model. Jest runs and reports both, so the coverage is intact.
findings.none: Cosmetic. A follow-up can give the no-model case its own title.

findings.finding: Chunk data is parsed as unknown and validated with a zod safeParse in reportedModel, and the test parses request bodies with zod. A grep of the diff and identity.test.ts found no as casts, no any, and no non-null assertions.
findings.none: The boundary already parses its input.

findings.finding: The log uses console.info with a fixed key=value line. The server has no structured logger and already logs through console.warn in api.ts and console.error in models.ts, so the line follows local style and holds only ids.
reply and generate take seven positional parameters. That is the existing Providers.generate interface in provider.ts, and the new method copies it.
findings.none: Changing the shared interface is outside this change.

findings.finding: The only colon in the new docs section introduces the log format example, which the rule allows. The section has no dashes as separators.

The section names its actors in the active voice: the server logs one line, and a Responses request sends the line as instructions. The one passive-style sentence says the line is not part of the input items, which describes a state, not an action.
